title: Chapter 3: The Former Protagonist and the Former Villain 1
content: "Next month is summer vacation, so let's enjoy ourselves while we can, okay?"
"Yeah, but the crowd is really something."
As we chatted, I walked with Alicia down the bustling main street.
It was already early summer, and summer vacation would begin in August.
We had decided to spend it in Brave Territory, so our time in the Royal Capital wouldn't be that long.
With the intention of making the most of our limited time, we had come out on a date together.
I recalled Alicia from this morning.
"Let's go to the town, I'll show you around today."
"So, does that mean it's a date?"
"That's right. I'll also buy some seeds for gardening and my vegetable patch."
Her enthusiastic nodding was brave, and the fragility she had when we first met was long gone.
But I was secretly pleased that she said our date wasn't just a side note to her errands.
You might wonder about the concept of August and holidays in another world, but in this otome game world, people follow a calendar established by the Ancient Sage.
A year runs from January to December, and a week consists of seven days from Monday to Sunday, complete with an actual calendar.
As you might guess, the Ancient Sage refers to the game developers.

The game boasted a system where events in the town changed based on the day of the week, significantly altering the progression of flags, which likely led them to incorporate it even if it broke the world's immersion.

In the game, there were often scenes where characters would bump into each other in town, but imagining high-ranking nobles casually strolling around pretending to have a chance encounter is just hilarious.

By the way, if you head to town on Friday the 13th, you'll encounter a mysterious figure wearing Jason's mask and get caught up in a dangerous incident, which boosts your favorability rating dramatically if you overcome it, along with a special illustration.
"Alicia, I've also found the location of that food stall you seemed interested in, so let's stop by on our way back?"
"Is that okay?"
"Today, it's my turn to guide you, so leave it to me. There are quite a lot of people compared to Brave Territory, so you might get overwhelmed."
"That's not true. When we were ambushed at night, I couldn't tell if the people around me were allies, enemy soldiers, or corpses; it was that crowded."
Compared to that, the daytime crowd was nothing.
"Ah, yeah, you're right."
"W-What did you say...?"
I was lightly brushed off, wasn't I!?
Alicia had begun to develop a tolerance for my Brave jokes.
As I was in shock, she narrowed her eyes and leaned closer.
"Don't say that to anyone else."
It's my only humor, and what a bummer.
But her request to keep it between us felt oddly comforting.
Woof woof.
"By the way, if you go straight here and turn into the alley, there's a place that serves delicious coffee, so let's have lunch there?"
"Oh, that sounds interesting."
Since coffee wasn't available at the noble academy, I had been worried about what to do once the supply I brought ran out.
I thought I could find some in the town, but I was overwhelmed with gratitude that Alicia had already done the searching for me.
"Alicia, where did you get that information?"
"A friend told me."
W-What did you say...?
As I expected, Alicia and I were treated like outcasts at the academy, but we were managing just fine, attending classes, taking tests, and graduating, so it didn't really matter.
For her to make friends in that situation, she truly was a talented girl.
I still felt like a loner, and I wished I could at least get to know Mariana, but I wouldn't even know how to approach her without Sebas pushing me from behind.
I wasn't jealous or anything! In fact, I was proud.
I'll check later to see what kind of ulterior motives she might have.
"I was studying in the library with the coffee I brought when I was approached by that girl. She was also worried that there was no coffee at the academy, and we became friends from there."
"Wow."
When asked if she liked coffee, Alicia replied that it was surprisingly delicious, and before she knew it, they had become friends, and she had been introduced to a recommended shop.
There are some interesting people out there, in more ways than one.
"The coffee problem is important, so this is a blessing in disguise."
"Yeah, I can't start my day without coffee."
Both of us were proud caffeine addicts.
"Ah, by the way, she's a girl, so don't worry!"
"I'm not worried. In fact, I'm more relieved that there's nothing to worry about!"
We exchanged such banter and ended up bursting into laughter together.
It was peaceful, truly peaceful.
"Here it is."
Turning off the main street into a narrow side road, Alicia pointed to a building.
"Um... Coffee Specialty Store, Ocean...?"
I froze as I read the sign.
I had no memory of the protagonist opening a café in the game.
If such a setting existed, there should have been an event for it.
It had become a popular café for handsome guys to gather, and somehow coffee had permeated the noble class... that can't happen; it would make it impossible to buy cheaply, so that's a no-go.
"Are you just browsing? Oh, isn't that Alicia?"
"Here I am, Mariana."
As I stood frozen in front of the store, Mariana opened the door and poked her head out.
Just sharing the same last name didn't mean this was the store run by the former protagonist, I thought, but it turned out to be Mariana Ocean.
The two of them called each other by their first names, and Mariana's confident demeanor was a stark contrast to how she had been in class.
Before nobles, she had been excessively humble, and now there was a world of difference.
"Is that the one who loves coffee?"
"Yes, this is Lagna."
It seemed my introduction had already been taken care of, and the conversation flowed smoothly.
"I'm Lagna, nice to meet you."
"Nice to meet you... Wait, hmm? Are you in the same class?"
Mariana squinted and adjusted her glasses, looking at me intently.
"Is that so? What an unexpected connection."
"Yeah, we haven't talked before, though."
Nodding at Alicia's words, Mariana suddenly turned pale and began to panic.
"I-I-I'm so sorry! I never expected to be with a noble!"
"Eh?"
Alicia's eyes widened at her sudden words.
"W-W-W-Will there be something that suits your palate here...?"
"Lagna, what did you do?"
"Eh?"
Alicia glared at me, clearly flustered, but I hadn't done anything!
I had just been observing quietly so as not to get caught.
"Why are you with a noble...?"
"Eh, noble? He's my fiancé."
"Noble!? Eek! Please forgive my rudeness!"
The moment Alicia answered, Mariana was bowing deeply.
She rubbed her forehead against the floor, performing a perfect dogeza.
"I'm so sorry! I didn't know you were a noble!"
"Eh!? Please stop! This is embarrassing!"
"Ah, ah, ah, I'm so sorry, I'm so sorry, I'm so sorry!"
"Hey, please! Look up, I'm begging you! Lagna, do something!"
"I can't."
I didn't know what had caused this, but Mariana Ocean was someone who would bend over backwards for nobles, so we had no choice but to wait until she calmed down.
I thought she was different from the girl I knew in class, but it seemed she simply hadn't recognized Alicia as a noble.
"Is this a crime of disrespect? Will I be punished? Oh no, Mom and Dad, I'm coming to join you right now!"
"I won't punish you! There's no way I would do that! Stop rolling your eyes and come back to reality! Please!"
"Bubububububu."
"Lagna! She's foaming at the mouth! W-What should we do!?"
Haha, chaos.
"Is she going to die!? Mariana, are you okay!? Is this alright!?"
"She won't die from that, so it's fine."
After that, Mariana kept waking up and fainting, finally calming down.
She was not just bad with nobles; she was allergic to them.
What a shame for the former protagonist.
"I'm sorry for losing my composure..."
Once she regained her calm, Mariana blushed while holding the coffee I brewed.
"I'm sorry too, I never expected things to turn out like this."

"Alicia isn't at fault. I heard there were two children of sages this year, so when I saw Alicia studying in the library with a coffee in hand, I completely misunderstood that she was the same as me."
Just like how Alicia had her first taste of coffee when she came to Brave Territory, the nobles in this world didn't drink coffee.
Nobles were supposed to enjoy tea, while coffee was a drink for commoners.
From that perspective, it was understandable that Mariana mistook her for another child of the sage.
Moreover, the fact that Alicia was studying alone in the library only added to the misunderstanding.
Naturally, nobles at the academy wouldn't be found sipping coffee alone in a corner of the library.
They would be socializing and focusing on tea parties.
"I tend to stand out at the academy, so I always act alone. I thought you would know the circumstances, so I'm sorry for not saying anything."
"Don't worry about it. I was the one who suddenly approached you and started rambling about coffee... I was just excited that I might finally make a friend..."
"I was also excited to talk a lot about coffee since Lagna is the only one I have now..."
The two of them continued to apologize to each other like this.
They were a perfect match, weren't they?
I felt a twinge of jealousy, as I was completely out of the picture.
"Mariana, so we're good now, right?"
"Yes, there's no bad person who loves coffee!"
I'm glad they made up.
"But I never expected a fellow child of the sage to cause such an incident... I thought only attending the academy was permitted..."
After hearing about the duel incident from Alicia, Mariana's cheerful smile turned into a pained expression.
The reason she hadn't known about the duel commotion was that the shared carriage she used to attend the academy had inexplicably set off toward the outskirts of the Royal Capital.
"I've always been a bit directionally challenged, but I never thought I would get on the wrong carriage. Even though I always use the same one, I keep making mistakes..."
Mariana tilted her head, but it seemed like someone was plotting against her.
That someone was Patricia.
She was keeping her away from important events.
"You're surprisingly absent-minded, huh? I thought being a child of the sage meant you were some kind of genius."
"I'm good at magic! But my parents often told me to ask for help with everything else since I'm a bit of a klutz."
The protagonist was intentionally designed to be a bit of a klutz for the sake of the story.
They would miss important lines but be sharp in unexpected areas.
"By the way, how are your parents?"
I decided to join their conversation, asking something that had been on my mind.
"My parents... they passed away a year ago due to illness..."
"Lagna... you..."
Alicia, who had been looking down, glared at me with narrowed eyes.
"I was inconsiderate; I'm sorry."
I regretted stepping on a landmine.
But more than that, I was horrified by the fact that Alicia always carried a collar with her.
"It's fine. I am who I am now thanks to my parents."
As I sincerely apologized, Mariana stood up and headed to the counter, preparing some sweets on a plate while continuing to speak.
"Would you both like a refill on your coffee? I invited you, but I'm sorry for making Lagna brew it."
"Can I have some? I'll pay properly."
"I'll take it. Please."
We were lightly shocked by the coffee and cake that were served.
"Wow! This is delicious!"
"What's different from mine...?"
It should have been the same beans, but what was this richness?
My coffee had once been described as harsh by Sebas.
He had said something like it represented the young master's life.
After a lot of practice, I had learned to soften it with milk and sugar, but even then, the black coffee still had a mysterious bitterness.
No wonder Alicia had coughed the first time she drank it.
In contrast, Mariana's coffee had a richness that enveloped you like a holy mother.
I know it sounds strange, but that's the only way I can express it.
"There's a huge difference from what Lagna brewed! Mariana, you're amazing!"
"Eh?"
Is there really a need to compare me to her?
Mariana is a professional running a specialty store!
She really has started to resemble the people of the Brave Family...
"Fufu, Lagna's coffee is still lacking! It's harsh!"
Even Mariana joined in, and I wasn't even aiming to become a professional, but both of them were saying some harsh things.
Since Mariana's presence is essential for the plot, maybe I should just become her apprentice.
"Then I'll call you my master, Coffee Master."
I am a disliked noble, and Mariana has an allergy to nobles.
I am grateful to Alicia for turning a negative start into a positive one.
"Eh, no, I just said that jokingly, and you're taking it so seriously..."
"Oh, Lagna, you don't have to take it seriously either since it was just a joke."
"Eh!? Is that so!?"
"Hahaha."
I laughed it off, but I would insist on calling her master from now on.
It was a perfect opportunity to learn about coffee.
"But it's strange. Even though you two are nobles, you don't seem scary at all."
After laughing for a while, Mariana spoke while sipping her coffee.

"I have a vague memory... but when I was little, a neighbor kid told me that nobles are terrifying beings, and if you oppose them, you'll be killed. It's a very hazy memory, but I always thought that."
It's not entirely wrong; there are indeed nobles like that.
"When I was small, I accidentally ran in front of a carriage carrying nobles and got hit, but just like that kid said, I wasn't helped. The carriage didn't even stop."
Alicia silently listened to Mariana's voice.
From her expression, it seemed she was thinking that her past self would likely ignore Mariana too.
That's just how it is.
Even in Brave Territory, if someone steps into a domain they shouldn't and gets counterattacked, the one who intruded is considered at fault.
"Ah, but you two aren't scary! There are no bad people who love coffee, and I respect you both for being in a tougher situation than I am!"
The adventurers in Brave Territory who drink coffee aren't necessarily good people, but I wonder who taught her that.
"Even if it was an accident, that's a terrible story. I'll apologize on behalf of the nobles; I'm sorry."
"Alicia, please don't apologize!"
"I ended up with poor eyesight due to the injuries from that time, but thanks to that, I met coffee!"
So the thick bottle-bottom glasses were a result of that injury.
It seems that rumors about coffee improving eyesight reached her parents, and that's how she started drinking it more often.
"I never thought my family would become coffee addicts to the point of opening a shop... hehehe, this richness, hehehe."
Scary.
Mariana, with her bottle-bottom glasses gleaming ominously as she savored the coffee, felt less like a protagonist and more like a coffee-loving monster.
"Hey, since you're called a child of the sage, does that mean your magic is amazing?"
While enjoying the richness, Alicia asked a very vague question.
Just like when I was asked, it seemed she sparkled with excitement when inquiring about magic.
If you're from a noble family in a country known for magic, I guess that's to be expected.
"Well, I'm decent at it. My specialty is healing magic."
"Being good at healing magic is pretty rare, right?"
"Yeah."
I quietly listened to the lively conversation between the two, occasionally joining in naturally.
It was fine to become completely invisible, but that would be lonely.
Returning to a serious topic.
Healing magic was actually one of the types of magic that anyone could use.
For the people living in this world, overflowing with magical energy, mere natural healing abilities were already at the level of magic.
However, that was merely a function standardly equipped in living beings.
The conversation changes when it comes to whether one can use it on others.
The reason it's considered rare is that very few people can use it on others.
In that context, the Mariana in the game, who was said to be a saint, could dispel all diseases and even restore lost limbs.
In combat, she could even enable the handsome guys to perform zombie attacks, but that's a different story that ends with significant drawbacks.
"At that time, I couldn't help my sick parents, and they told me to make sure I could save someone important if I ever had one again. So I studied a lot to enroll."
"Mariana, you..."
"Ah, Alicia!? Please don't cry!!"
"Uu, it's such a nice story..."
I joined in and pretended to cry along with Alicia, who was getting emotional.
"Speaking of which, Lagna, you can heal others too, right?"
"Yeah, but it's special, so I don't think it would be helpful."
"Is that so? Well, I guess it's Lagna, so that makes sense."
I tried to brush off Alicia's probing questions.
I had boasted to Volzeia that I could use it on everyone, and of course, I could use it on others.
The reason I brushed it off was that while healing magic might seem like a gentle power, it actually wasn't for a specific reason.
It's a special case, or rather, a reverse general case.
To reach the level of healing others, one must thoroughly understand human anatomy and visually comprehend the flow of magical energy within the body.
If you do that, while you won't be able to neatly heal missing limbs or scars, you can heal significant internal damage or reattach parts before they start to rot.
So how do you train for that? — Dissection.
The path of a warrior that is even better if done while alive.
Of course, there's no way such things could be done at the academy, and Mariana doesn't have a bloody past like that.
Because she's a saint, if she trains her magical power, she can recover various things without limits.
Ah, what a fake.
To me, a saint is a monster; what about you?
"By the way, there aren't any other customers, are there?"
Even while we were chatting, there were still only me and Alicia in the shop.
Alicia looked puzzled by the situation, but it was my fault.
"I'm sorry; I accidentally closed the shop since we were all flustered at first."
"Lagna..."
In her hand was the collar!
But really, there was no way to provide proper service in that initial state, so closing the shop for a bit was the normal thing to do.
That's why we could have such deep conversations; this was my brilliant decision.
"If you don't open soon, it will be considered obstructing business! Open up!"
"Woof woof!"
"Eh, woof woof...? W-What about the collar...?"
Mariana looked very confused by the situation between me and Alicia.
"You two are fine. Recently, I've wanted to focus on my studies, so I've been closing on holidays. I only opened today because I thought Alicia might come!"
As someone who lost her parents, balancing both studies and running a shop was impossible.
"Then how are you managing your tuition and living expenses? Since children of sages get various exemptions, wouldn't it have been better to stay in the dorm?"
"This house is nice, Alicia. It's not too far to commute, and since there's no coffee at the academy, I wouldn't choose to stay in the dorm either."
"That's true. I'm sorry; I was told to ask everything I didn't understand about the Brave Family, so I developed a habit of asking directly."
"Haha, I like straightforwardness. Just as Lagna said, I'm a commoner, so I declined the dorm."
Mariana laughed as she watched me and Alicia bicker.
I had stepped on a landmine, and Alicia was fine; it was a difference in status.
"For living expenses, the academy head kindly allocated some funds for dorm fees on the condition that I maintain good grades, so I'm managing."
That was a relief.
I was worried about what I would do if they said the Ignite family was supporting them, but it was unfounded anxiety.
"It's almost time... I'm really reluctant to leave."
Alicia stood up while looking at the clock.
We had various shopping to do, so it was time to leave the shop.
"The coffee and cake were delicious, can I come again?"
"If it's Alicia, you're always welcome!"
"Alright, Lagna, we've got the green light! Let's come here on weekends!"
"Y-Yeah."
As long as it doesn't become a nuisance, I suppose that's fine?
While enjoying delicious coffee, I could keep an eye on Mariana's movements and her surroundings, so it was a win-win.
"Alicia, if anything happens at the academy, please let me know anytime! I might be unreliable, but I was raised to help friends!"
"Fufu, just those words are enough. Thank you."
"Ah! Your smile is too dazzling, it's painful!"
I understand that feeling; I really do.
"Lagna, please give me Alicia."
"Absolutely not."
No matter how the world turns upside down or how disasters strike, I will never accept that.
"What are you suddenly saying... both of you..."
And so we left Mariana's shop.
"She's a good girl, isn't she? She seems a bit airheaded, but I think that's cute."
"Yeah."
As we walked down the street together, Alicia's expression was incredibly happy.
"When I first saw her, she had the same eyes as you."
It feels a bit off to compare her to the fallen nobility of the discarded land in the story, but I'll listen to her for now.
"She has a gaze that feels like it looks straight at you; such beautiful eyes."
"People with a strong core tend to have such eyes."
Those with strong will often possess such gazes.
I find those eyes to be the most beautiful of all.
"Enemies with a death-defying resolve have such beautiful eyes, don't they?"
"Mariana must be the same, considering how scared she is of nobles."
It was a light Brave joke, but once again, Alicia didn't get it.
I need to prepare a different joke; she might be getting bored with my humor.
"I've decided! I have to protect Mariana!"
While I was lost in my trivial thoughts, Alicia expressed her strong determination.
However, she suddenly stopped and looked at my face, saying,
"Hey, Lagna, how do my eyes look?"
"Hmm, they're more beautiful than any eyes I've seen so far."
"Really? I was just realizing that I used to have murky eyes!"
For nobles who value their reputation, exposing themselves to ridicule in front of the public is more terrifying than death.
You can't endure this hellish situation without a strong will.
That's why I think Alicia is strong.
"What do you think about someone facing difficulties?"
"I think it's really cool."
"Then how beautiful must their eyes be when you see them from the front?"
"Lagna, have you ever seen someone like that?"
"I have."
I stood in front of Alicia and met her gaze.
"They have eyes filled with an incredibly strong will, beautiful and cute."
When I said that honestly, her face turned bright red.
"If you didn't say such weird jokes, you'd really be like a prince."
"That's not my style."
I can't say sweet nothings that would make all women happy, especially since I still don't have any male friends.
"That's true; Lagna is Lagna. Now, shall we continue our date?"
I took Alicia's outstretched hand and we began walking together again.
